chunks: We could send down from the heavens a sign to them if We pleased, before which their heads would remain bowed.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean when God sends a sign from the heavens and people bow their necks?
ai.summary: In the context of Surah Ash-Shu'ara, this verse underscores the divine prerogative to compel belief through overwhelming signs, contrasting with the usual human tendency to reject them despite clear evidence. Shia exegesis often highlights this as a demonstration of God's absolute power (Qudrah) to guide those He wills, serving as a rhetorical challenge to the disbelievers of Mecca who demanded miraculous proofs.
